product.name: Z-axis
product.introText: The Z-axis of the FarmBot Genesis v1.5: the one-metre extrusion with its motor, leadscrew, cable carrier supports and vacuum pump, built lying on the bench and then lowered through the V-wheels of the finished cross-slide. Steps, text and pictures are from the FarmBot Genesis v1.5 documentation, the parts are from its CAD model; both are published by FarmBot Inc. under the CC0 Public Domain Dedication. This site is not affiliated with or endorsed by FarmBot Inc.
product.partsSummary: 1 z-axis extrusion (20 x 20 x 1000mm), 1 z-axis motor mount, 1 stepper motor, 4 M3 screws, 2 60mm nut bars, 4 40mm nut bars, 16 M5 x 10mm screws, 2 M5 x 16mm screws, 1 shaft coupling with 4 screws, 4 cable carrier supports, 6 M5 tee nuts, 1 vacuum pump cover, 1 vacuum pump with mount, 1 leadscrew, 2 hardstops, 1 vertical motor housing, and the finished cross-slide.  Not shown: 2 zip ties; tools (2.5mm hex key, 3mm hex driver).

steps.title: Attach the stepper motor to the Z-axis motor mount
steps.text: Attach a stepper motor to the z-axis motor mount using four M3 x 12mm screws. The motor and encoder connectors should be facing the back flange of the mount.

moves.label: z-axis motor mount
stepper motor, connectors towards the back flange
4x M3 screw

steps.title: Attach the motor mount to the Z-axis extrusion
steps.text: Handle with care: the aluminum extrusions may have sharp corners and edges. Attach the z-axis motor mount to the z-axis extrusion using a 60mm nut bar and M5 x 10mm screws. The top face of the motor mount should be 80mm from the end of the extrusion.

moves.label: 2x M5 x 10mm screw through the mount
60mm nut bar, loosely on the screws
z-axis extrusion onto the nut bar - mount 80mm from the end

steps.title: Attach the shaft coupling
steps.text: Slide the 5mm to 8mm shaft coupling onto the motor shaft and tighten the top screw with the 2.5mm hex key. Mind the gap: make sure there is a small gap (about 2mm) between the shaft coupling and the z-axis motor mount. You might use a credit card to help provide the correct spacing needed. [The coupling's lower screws are put in here too; they are tightened in step 8.]

moves.label: 5mm to 8mm shaft coupling
2x coupling screw - 2.5mm hex key
2x coupling screw - 2.5mm hex key

steps.title: Attach three cable carrier supports
steps.text: Attach three 60mm vertical cable carrier supports to the z-axis extrusion using 40mm nut bars and M5 x 10mm screws. Space the supports along the extrusion as shown.

moves.label: 2x M5 x 10mm screw through the support
40mm nut bar, loosely on the screws
60mm vertical cable carrier support - slide the nut bar into the slot
2x M5 x 10mm screw through the support
40mm nut bar, loosely on the screws
60mm vertical cable carrier support - slide the nut bar into the slot
2x M5 x 10mm screw through the support
40mm nut bar, loosely on the screws
60mm vertical cable carrier support - slide the nut bar into the slot

steps.title: Attach the vacuum pump cover
steps.text: Attach the vacuum pump cover to the z-axis extrusion using two M5 drop-in tee nuts and M5 x 10mm screws. The cover should be butted up against the lowest cable carrier support.

moves.label: 2x M5 drop-in tee nut
vacuum pump cover, against the lowest support
2x M5 x 10mm screw

steps.title: Attach the vacuum pump
steps.text: Fasten the vacuum pump to the vacuum pump mount using two 200mm zip ties. Then attach the vacuum pump mount to the z-axis extrusion using a 60mm nut bar and two M5 x 16mm screws. The mount should be butted up against the vacuum pump cover. [Not shown here: the two zip ties.]

moves.label: vacuum pump onto its mount (two 200mm zip ties, not shown)
2x M5 x 16mm screw through the mount
60mm nut bar, loosely on the screws
vacuum pump mount - slide the nut bar into the slot, up to the cover

steps.title: Attach one more cable carrier support
steps.text: Attach one more 60mm vertical cable carrier support using a 40mm nut bar and two M5 x 10mm screws. The support should be butted up against the vacuum pump mount.

moves.label: 2x M5 x 10mm screw through the support
40mm nut bar, loosely on the screws
60mm vertical cable carrier support - slide the nut bar into the slot

steps.title: Attach the z-axis to the cross-slide
steps.text: Screw the leadscrew halfway into the leadscrew block. Slide the z-axis extrusion through the v-wheels on the cross-slide until the leadscrew inserts into the 5mm to 8mm shaft coupling. Then tighten the coupling's lower screw with the 2.5mm hex key. Adjust the eccentric spacers as needed: in order to slide the z-axis through the v-wheels you will need to adjust the eccentric spacers of the three v-wheels on the right side of the cross-slide. Refer to the eccentric spacer adjustment reference guide for how to do this. [Here the finished cross-slide is one part and hangs in the air where the gantry main beam would hold it; adjusting and tightening are not shown.]

moves.label: finished cross-slide
leadscrew - screw it halfway into the leadscrew block

steps.title: Install the hardstops
steps.text: Attach the z-axis hardstops onto the backside of the z-axis extrusion approximately 200mm from the top of the extrusion and 100mm from the bottom of the extrusion using M5 x 10mm screws and tee nuts. Later, you can quickly adjust these to physically prevent FarmBot from moving too low or too hight within its working space.

moves.label: 2x M5 tee nut
2x z-axis hardstop
2x M5 x 10mm screw

steps.title: Add the vertical motor housing (optional)
steps.text: If you plan on stopping assembly after this page, it is recommended to attach the 80mm vertical motor housing to the z-axis extrusion using M5 x 10mm screws and tee nuts now. This will protect the motor from rain and other hazards until you resume assembly at a later point. Once you resume assembly, you will need to remove the housing. If you do not plan on stopping the assembly process now, you can skip this step and install the housing after the z motor and encoder cables have been connected in the next step.

moves.label: 2x M5 tee nut
80mm vertical motor housing
2x M5 x 10mm screw
